statement: Let n = len(stones). The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Call a finite sequence of indices i_0, i_1, ..., i_m a valid crossing when: m >= 1; i_0 = 0; i_m = n - 1; 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_m < n; and, writing d_t = stones[i_t] - stones[i_{t-1}] for t = 1, ..., m, we have d_1 = 1 and for every t with 2 <= t <= m, d_t > 0 and d_t is either d_{t-1} - 1, d_{t-1}, or d_{t-1} + 1. Then r = true if and only if there exists a valid crossing; equivalently, r = false if and only if no valid crossing exists.
preconditions: Let n = len(stones). 2 <= n <= 2000; stones[0] = 0; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= stones[i] <= 2^31 - 1; for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, stones[i] < stones[i + 1].
